source_name: Cornerstone International Group — Budapest office
why_relevant: Retained executive search network with a Budapest presence; a further node for HU senior-appointment signals in financial services. Lower priority than Amrop/Stanton Chase given smaller apparent HU footprint.

source_name: Friisberg & Partners International — Hungary
why_relevant: Search network claiming a BBJ-based No.1 executive-search position in Hungary. The claim itself is a marketing assertion and conflicts with the HumanField/ISG rankings seen elsewhere, which makes it a useful cross-check on how contested these HU rankings are — and a further mandate-signal node.

source_name: Pénzcentrum — karrier/HR desk (recruiter-report amplification channel)
why_relevant: Hungarian consumer-finance outlet that systematically covers and often mirrors recruiter salary guides (it hosts the full Hays 2026 PDF). The fastest way to learn a new HU recruiter report exists, and often the only ungated route to its contents.

source_name: Ravio — Hungary salary benchmarks
why_relevant: Payroll-data-based compensation benchmarking platform publishing a Hungary page. Not a recruiter, but an adjacent labour-market analyst whose data is derived from live payroll rather than recruiter self-report — a valuable independent check on Hays/Randstad numbers for finance and tech roles.

source_name: Clutch.co — Top Recruiting Firms in Hungary directory
why_relevant: A crowd-reviewed directory that enumerates HU recruiting and HR firms beyond the BBJ revenue list, including smaller boutique and fintech-focused shops the paid rankings miss. Reviews are self-selected and promotional, so use it purely as an actor-discovery pointer, not as an evidence source.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — Tagjaink (member bank directory)
why_relevant: Canonical enumeration of ~67 Hungarian credit institutions (full members, associated members, observers incl. GIRO Zrt., Magyar Államkincstár, OBA, Diákhitel Központ). Cheapest single expansion of the banking entity universe for every other A5 cell; each member has a detail page (tagreszlet.cshtml?tagId=NN) that yields the institution's own site and contact person.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — Szervezet (Elnökség / governance pages)
why_relevant: Names the Association's own presidency and supervisory board — each seat is held by a named senior executive of a named bank (e.g. president from Erste, vice-president from OTP Jelzálogbank, FB chair from K&H, members from CIB, UniCredit, Raiffeisen, MBH, Gránit, ING, Bank of China, Citibank branch, GIRO). Triennial tisztújítás makes this a dated leadership-move signal AND a who-runs-which-bank cross-reference.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — Munkacsoportok (working groups)
why_relevant: Working groups (payments, cards, IT/cyber, compliance, etc.) are chaired by named bank specialists — a directory of mid-level subject-matter owners across all member banks. Very high value for A5 'who does what' mapping, since these names are the practical counterparties for payments/vendor topics and their rotation signals internal reorganisations.

source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség (MAFISZ / Hungarian Fintech Association) — tagok + igazgatóság
why_relevant: Enumerates the ~30+ Hungarian fintech / payment-institution / regtech companies (e.g. Barion, Dorsum, SEON) that no bank-centric list captures, and the homepage names the board (elnök Ács Zoltán; board incl. Barion founder-CEO Kiss Sándor; főtitkár dr. Urbán Viktor). Two-year board mandates give a recurring leadership-move event.

source_name: IVSZ — Szövetség a Digitális Gazdaságért: tagvállalatok + szervezeti felépítés
why_relevant: The ICT-industry association's member directory is the vendor-side counterpart to the bank list — it includes fintech and payments vendors (individual member profile pages, e.g. /tagvallalatok/zelig-fintech/). Its Fintech Munkacsoport and its elnökség elections (SME / micro / startup-scaleup seats) are documented on-site.

source_name: AmCham Hungary — Board of Directors & committee structure
why_relevant: Annual (December) general-assembly board elections are published with full name/title/company for each director and the supervisory board chair (2024 cycle: president Ákos Janza, MSCI; directors incl. Morgan Stanley Hungary Analytics' head of risk). AmCham committees are the venue where financial-services country managers surface publicly, so committee pages act as a pointer to FS leadership.

source_name: HBLF — Hungarian Business Leaders Forum: elnökség + member companies
why_relevant: Board seats are filled by named senior executives of member corporations, and the member-company directory contains bank entries with their own profile pages (e.g. ING Bank N.V. Magyarországi Fióktelepe). A public call for nominations for the president and 5 board seats expiring in 2026 was observed — a scheduled, trackable leadership event.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség (Hungarian Leasing Association) — Kik vagyunk? + hírek
why_relevant: ~36 asset-finance member companies — bank-owned leasing arms (Merkantil/OTP, Raiffeisen Corporate Leasing, MKB-Euroleasing, SG Eszközfinanszírozás, Ayvens/LeasePlan) that are invisible in the banking-association list. Publishes its own board changes as dated news items (e.g. 'Új alelnök és elnökségi tagok a Magyar Lízingszövetségnél'), and each board seat identifies a named executive's current employer.

source_name: MABISZ — Magyar Biztosítók Szövetsége (governance + members)
why_relevant: Adjacent-sector body (~30 insurers, many bancassurance partners of HU banks). Elects an eight-member elnökség which then elects president/vice-president (March 2025: NN's Holló Bence replacing Generali's Erdős Mihály) — a clean, dated leadership-move stream naming insurer CEOs. Its published Alapszabály documents the election mechanics and cadence.

source_name: MAKISZ — Magyar Követeléskezelők és Üzleti Információt Szolgáltatók Szövetsége
why_relevant: Enumerates the debt-collection / business-information firms that sit downstream of every HU bank's NPL portfolio — an entity class absent from bank, fintech and IT association lists. The 'szovetseg' section carries the organisational description and officers.

source_name: Blockchain Magyarország Egyesület
why_relevant: Founded September 2018; the crypto/DLT-side professional body whose membership overlaps HU payment startups and PSP vendors. Useful for enumerating the digital-asset actor set that neither MAFISZ nor IVSZ fully covers; 'Rólunk' page is the officer/board entry point.

source_name: Blockchain Koalíció (state-initiated coalition, chaired by Vágujhelyi Ferenc)
source_subtype: trade-press coverage of a quasi-official body
why_relevant: Formed 8 March 2022 on the initiative of the innovation ministry and the national data-economy knowledge centre; its chairmanship links state digitalisation bodies to payments/DLT industry actors. Currently only reachable through trade-press coverage — a quasi-official body without an obvious standalone portal, so the interview article is the anchor for further tracing.

source_name: Portfolio.hu — banking association / leadership tag pages
why_relevant: The most reliable HU financial daily for association tisztújítás reporting; its articles list the full elected board with bank affiliations (2020 and 2023 cycles both covered) and its cimke (tag) pages act as pre-built chronologies per association, e.g. the Magyar Lízingszövetség tag. Useful as a corroboration layer and for back-filling history the associations themselves do not archive.

source_name: FinTechZone.hu — Hungarian fintech trade portal
why_relevant: Covers MAFISZ partnerships, membership growth and board interviews in more depth than the association's own site; a practical early-warning channel for fintech-side appointments and for new entrants joining the association.

source_name: Fintech.hu — Magyar Fintech Szövetség tag archive
why_relevant: A ready-made chronological archive of MAFISZ items including the presidential change announcement ('Új elnök a Magyar Fintech Szövetség élén') — cheapest way to reconstruct the association's leadership timeline without crawling the association site's history.

source_name: Budapest Business Journal — Chamber of Commerce Corner
why_relevant: A recurring English-language column that aggregates news from ALL the foreign chambers in Hungary (AmCham, BCCH, DUIHK, JVSZ and others) in one place — including leadership announcements and committee activity. The single cheapest way to monitor the chamber layer without crawling each chamber separately.

source_name: BCCH — British Chamber of Commerce in Hungary: Management page
why_relevant: Names the chamber's board and management; UK-linked banks, PSPs and professional-services firms sit on it, so board turnover doubles as an executive-move signal for those firms. Complements AmCham for the non-US foreign-investor layer.

source_name: DUIHK / AHK Ungarn — German-Hungarian Chamber of Industry and Commerce
why_relevant: Largest bilateral chamber in Hungary; German-owned financial actors and IT/payments vendors are members, and the chamber publishes its Vorstand/elnökség and member directory. Reached here via the AHK network hub, which is the stable entry point to the Hungarian chapter's own domain.

source_name: MNB Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület — A Testület (member/officer page)
why_relevant: The clearest example of an MNB-affiliated body that publishes its own composition: the PBT's members are MNB employees (chair excepted) organised into two tanácsok, and its annual activity report is a recurring official publication. Gives named, dated appointments inside the supervisory perimeter — the regulator-side analogue of an association board.

source_name: KiberPajzs consortium (MNB + Magyar Bankszövetség + NMHH + NBSZ-NKI + ORFK)
why_relevant: A standing cross-institutional programme (agreed 7 Nov 2022) whose signatories and spokespeople are named — it maps which institution owns financial-cybercrime/payments-fraud policy and who represents each. Institution-change and representative-change signals appear in its joint communiqués.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — Hitelintézeti Szemle / publications
why_relevant: Author affiliations in the association's professional publications and speaker CVs hosted on the site (e.g. the secretary-general's GeP szakmai önéletrajz PDF) provide verified, dated role histories for HU banking figures — a cheap biographical backfill layer for leadership-move records.

source_name: OTP Bank corporate newsroom — association mandate announcements
why_relevant: Member banks publish their own executives' association appointments on their corporate newsrooms (here OTP on the Bankszövetség tisztújítás). Illustrates a repeatable pattern: for every bank on the member list, its /hirek newsroom is a corroborating and sometimes earlier source for association-seat leadership moves.
